      <title>US inflation rose 0.4% in October as price increases cooled and gas costs dipped</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/october-inflation-report</link>
      <description><p>New data comes after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices</p><p>US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month.</p><p>The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year-over-year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/october-inflation-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/oil-prices-fall-donald-trump-iran-war-ftse-100-markets</link>
      <description><p>Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes</p><p>Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/trump-iran-war">Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”</a>.</p><p>Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/oil-prices-fall-donald-trump-iran-war-ftse-100-markets">Continue reading...</a></description>
